overall.summary: LIQT's latest 10-Q shows a meaningful reduction in disclosure specificity, particularly around liquidity/going-concern projections and quantification of FX and macroeconomic exposures. The removal of the 12-month cash sufficiency statement and geographic operational detail, combined with the lack of quantified currency impacts relative to peers, suggests the company is becoming less transparent on topics where it previously provided useful detail. Two flags are dismissed as misattributed or relocated content, but the remaining concerns are substantive.
top_concerns: Disappearance of the 12-month cash sufficiency/liquidity adequacy statement that was present in the prior quarter filing — potential going-concern signal
Lack of quantified FX and tariff impact disclosure despite material international operations, in contrast to both prior filings and close peers
Minimal supply chain risk discussion despite operating across Denmark and China in a tariff-sensitive industrial sector
